item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00288","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C21","C07","C15"],"selected_candidate_label":"C21","confidence":0.83,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C21 plausibly supplied a material template for the child's treatment of federally created commissions governing interstate transportation. Both texts first acknowledge a genuine transportation problem, then reject the proposed federal commission because it inadequately respects State responsibilities and creates defective administrative arrangements, and finally identify an interstate compact or cooperative State arrangement as the preferable mechanism. C07 and C15 share the narrower idea that action affecting interstate waters should await agreement among affected governments, but they lack the child's commission-centered legal and administrative analysis.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The construction and operation of interstate bridges ... has traditionally been a State rather than a Federal responsibility.","parent_excerpt":"This bill is also unsatisfactory because it extends, without sufficient safeguards, the authority of the Federal Government to matters that have, hitherto, been considered as primarily the concern of the District of Columbia and of the States.","explanation":"Both frame the objection as inappropriate federal displacement of traditional State responsibility for regional transportation."},{"child_excerpt":"In those cases in which the States choose to create special interstate agencies to build, maintain and operate toll bridges, they may do so at any time through the negotiation of suitable interstate compacts.","parent_excerpt":"Specifically, provision should be made to enable the States of Maryland and Virginia and the District of Columbia eventually to make arrangements for the exercise of this function under joint responsibility. In this regard, it would appear desirable to explore the feasibility of utilizing an interstate compact or other cooperative arrangement","explanation":"The same concrete administrative alternative—joint State responsibility implemented through an interstate compact—is adapted from metropolitan transit regulation to interstate bridges."},{"child_excerpt":"Bridge commissions of the type provided for by these bills also give rise to serious legal and administrative problems.","parent_excerpt":"The present enactment, however, falls substantially short of this objective.... a system of fragmented and divided regulatory authority is continued.","explanation":"Both reject a transportation commission by moving from the underlying need to defects in the commission's jurisdiction, accountability, and administrative structure."}]}
